confirmed.prior_ref: The new 'could not remove N neighbourhood objects' warning is overwritten in the panel by every caller's next say(); sync_context then says 'Neighbourhood removed' although objects were left
confirmed.title: Round-6 fix put `return left` in the middle of _clear_context: the record delete, live-guide pop and dirty restore below it are now unreachable
confirmed.detail: 9674ca4 replaced `if left: say(...)` with `return left` but left the function's tail after it. So a full clear (sources=None, which is what sync_context does for the clear, draw and off steps) still deletes the objects but no longer deletes the neighbourhood record (doc.Strings CONTEXT_ENTRY), no longer drops STATE['context_guides'] and no longer puts back STATE['dirty']. What an architect sees: (1) step 'clear' (Edit site... to a lot the lookup didn't draw): the record keeps the old frame, so on every later box Draw context_step(None, drawn=old, on) returns 'clear' again and the panel says 'Neighbourhood removed' over and over, although nothing is drawn. (2) step 'off' (new lot looked up with the tick off) and step 'draw' when the fetch then fails: the old lot's record stays, so needs_refetch(held, old_record, ...) sees found layers and returns False. Ticking 'Show neighbourhood' then says 'Neighbourhood shown' and fetches nothing for the new lot (before round 6 the record was deleted, needs_refetch returned True and the new lot's neighbourhood was fetched). (3) Any live-only guides held for the doc stay in STATE, so draw_scene/bounds keep drawing the removed neighbourhood's footprints. (4) In live mode, sync_context's clear leaves the model marked 'changed since the check' (stale(): the result on screen is hidden until a re-check). This doesn't cause a false pass, because context layers are never measured, but the panel and drawing are wrong. CI can't catch it: the tests only look for these strings in the source text (they are still there, just unreachable), and the new round-6 test runs sync_context's 'clear' step without checking the record or STATE.
confirmed.pin: A new behavioural test in packages/design_checker/tests/test_context_box.py, using _clear_ns() and _context_doc() with a Strings.Delete that records its calls, ns['STATE'] = {'context_guides': {'doc': DOC, 'lines': [1]}, 'dirty': 5}, and a Delete that sets STATE['dirty'] = 9. After ns['_clear_context'](doc) it asserts all of: the return value is the refused count; ('gordium', logic.CONTEXT_ENTRY) is in the recorded deletes; 'context_guides' is not in STATE; STATE['dirty'] == 5. A second assert runs ns['_clear_context'](doc, {'nys_parcels'}) and checks the record is NOT deleted. Moving the return back above the tail must make this test fail. Optionally, also add an AST check that no function in gordium_rhino.py has statements after a return.
confirmed.suggested_fix:
Move the return to the end of the function, after the tail:
    _lock_context(doc, True)
    if sources is None:
        if logic.guides_of(STATE.get("context_guides"), doc.RuntimeSerialNumber):
            STATE.pop("context_guides", None)
        doc.Strings.Delete(SECTION, logic.CONTEXT_ENTRY)
    STATE["dirty"] = dirty
    return left
Then replace the string-presence asserts (lines 566 and 839) with the behavioural test above. Execute the code; don't search its text.
skeptics:
I could not refute this. The finding is real and was introduced on this branch. In apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_rhino.py, line 2516 (`return left`) sits in _clear_context before the tail at lines 2517-2521: `if sources is None:` pops STATE['context_guides'], runs doc.Strings.Delete(SECTION, logic.CONTEXT_ENTRY), then sets STATE['dirty'] = dirty. That tail can never run now. The line is new on this branch: `git diff origin/start-box-lookup...HEAD` shows `+    return left` followed by the added tail lines (commit 9674ca4).

Nothing upstream makes up for it. sync_context (lines ~2663-2672) calls `left = _clear_context(doc)` for the steps 'clear', 'draw' and 'off', then only calls draw_context or say(). It never deletes CONTEXT_ENTRY itself and never restores 'dirty'.

draw_context (lines ~2596-2637) does write the record again with doc.Strings.SetString. But that only happens when the fetch works. On the 'off' and 'clear' steps, and on a 'draw' whose fetch fails, the old record stays. Lines 2657 and 2710 then pass it to needs_refetch, so the stale-record outcomes the finding describes follow.

The pass with sources (line 2603) is not affected, because the tail was gated on sources being None anyway. The full-clear behaviour is broken as claimed.

I could not refute this; the bug is real. In apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_rhino.py:2516, `_clear_context` now has `return left` right after `_lock_context(doc, True)`. The lines below it (2517-2521) can never run: the `if sources is None:` block that pops STATE['context_guides'] and calls doc.Strings.Delete(SECTION, logic.CONTEXT_ENTRY), and `STATE["dirty"] = dirty`. On origin's parent commit a6a74ab, the same tail followed `if left: say(...)` and did run, so 9674ca4 introduced this.

No caller makes up for it. sync_context (2663-2665) calls `_clear_context(doc)` for the clear, draw and off steps and never deletes the record or pops the guides itself. The only other caller is draw_context (2596-2603), which passes `sources`. It does pop context_guides itself, but it relies on _clear_context to put the dirty mark back; its own comment at 2603 says so, and that now never happens either. The only other CONTEXT_ENTRY use is the read at 2540.

So `_context_record` keeps returning the old record. needs_refetch (2657, 2710) and context_step's `drawn` frame (2653) then see stale data, as the finding describes. The tests at test_context_box.py:566 and :839 only check that strings appear in the source text. They still pass because the dead code is still there.

priorStatus.title: The new 'could not remove N neighbourhood objects' warning is overwritten in the panel by every caller's next say(); sync_context then says 'Neighbourhood removed' although objects were left
priorStatus.reasoning: The warning itself is fixed. _clear_context no longer says anything and returns its refused count. Its only two callers put the count in their one line: sync_context sets `left = _clear_context(doc)`, passes it to draw_context(doc, frame, left), and wraps its 'off' and 'clear' lines in logic.with_not_cleared. draw_context adds `left += _clear_context(doc, sources)` and wraps all three of its say() calls (NO_CONTEXT, not found, drawn). with_not_cleared returns the text unchanged when the count is 0. grep finds no other caller of _clear_context. However, the same commit put `return left` before the function's tail, which is now unreachable. That is reported as a new P1 regression (see findings).
